title: Content labeling for automatic filtering for suicide prevention or other sensitive issues

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? The news sites are well aware that reporting on suicides has a negative impact on suicidal people. For this reason, news sites refer to suicide prevention centres as soon as they report on topics that are reminiscent of suicides. However, this obviously does not prevent people from being reminded of suicides. For this reason, I think it makes sense for website operators to be able to flag sensitive content so that browsers of affected persons can automatically filter out this content. ### What solutions exist today? I am not aware of any web standards that are used to filter content on a voluntary basis for suicide prevention or other sensitive issues. Website or platform operators refer to help centres or try to automatically identify relevant content in order to block or restrict it. ### How would you solve it? ### Step 1: Standardization of the labeling of sensitive content Website operators can voluntarily mark content for automatic filtering. E.g. by using the following meta tag to mark a website: `` Or by marking individual elements of a website: ```

Normal News

Filterable news

Normal News

``` ### Step 2: Standardisation of the setting option for automatic filtering of sensitive content People can set in the browser whether the browser should display sensitive content or not. ### Step 3: Automatic filtering Browser filters content without anyone knowing whether you have made the setting or not. ### Anything else? - It should not be possible for website operators to find out whether you have made the setting or not. - While the filtering of individual elements can be designed in such a way that filtering takes place unnoticed, this is not possible when filtering pages that are labelled as a whole. However, at least options can be implemented to prevent the content from being displayed immediately.
